Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for 2 months which began after a twisting injury. [REDACTED].
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Tricompartmental osteophytosis. Protuberant osteophytes extending into the femoral intercondylar notch. Inferior patellar enthesophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Small multiloculated leaking Baker's cyst with synovitis. 6 x 4 mm intra-articular body in the Baker's cyst. Fluid extends into the region of the pes anserinus 3 x 3 mm ossific intra-articular body at the anterolateral joint recess.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Intact.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing and posterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle with areas of high-grade cartilage loss and full-thickness fissuring. 

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Horizontal oblique undersurface tear at the posterior horn-body junction.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage loss at the posterior lateral femoral condyle with areas of full-thickness fissuring.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity at the patella and trochlea with large confluent regions of full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial patellar facet and full-thickness fissuring throughout the trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Mild proximal patellar tendinosis.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 16 mm, top-normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact. Fluid tracking into the popliteus muscle sheath.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Deep soft tissue edema at the posterior distal thigh. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, worst at the patellofemoral compartment, where it is severe. Moderate knee joint effusion. Small multiloculated leaking Baker's cyst with synovitis. Intra-articular bodies at the anterolateral joint recess and in the Baker's cyst.
2.	Horizontal oblique undersurface tear at the lateral meniscus posterior horn-body junction.
3.	Joint fluid decompression into the popliteus muscle sheath with synovitis.

МР находка: МР данни за минимален ставен излив. Костите, формиращи лявата колянна става са с непроменена форма. Слабо изразен костномозъчен едем в кондилите и епикондилите на тибията и фемура. Артикулиращият хрущял на фемура и тибията е съхранен. Без данни за руптура на предната кръстна връзка. Нормално представена задна кръстна връзка. Частична увреда на медиалния колатерален лигамент, който е с повишен сигнален интензитет в горния си сегмент.  Изобразява се увреда в задния рог на медиалния менискус – 3 степен. Нормално представен латерален менискус. Патела, хрущял на пателата, ретинакулуми – б.о.. Заключение:  МР данни за увреда на задния рог на медиалния менискус – 3 степен. Парциална увреда на медиален колатерален лигамент.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Meniscopatía degenerativa medial.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
El menisco lateral presenta fibrilación marginal de su cuerpo.
Rotura compleja de parte del cuerno anterior, cuerpo y cuerno posterior del menisco medial con parcial
desplazamiento de segmentos al receso menisco tibial a nivel del cuerpo y edema de las partes blandas
regionales.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial y prácticamente total de la zona de carga del compartimento
femorotibial medial sin cambios óseos secundarios. Condropatía superficial del compartimento femorotibial
lateral. Cartílago troclear con úlceras de espesor parcial de distribución difusa. Úlceras condrales de
espesor total con cambios óseos secundarios del vértice y faceta medial de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular con sinovitis difusa.
Aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital y de la inserción proximal del tendón
rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Rotura compleja del menisco medial con segmento parcialmente desplazado al receso menisco tibial a nivel
del cuerpo con edema de las partes blandas regionales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 y 3 del compartimento femorotibial medial.
Condropatía superficial del compartimento femorotibial lateral.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 de la tróclea femoral. Condropatía lesiones grado 4 de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular con sinovitis difusa.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital distal y rotuliana proximal.

Central supporting system  
  Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Abnormal high SI with thickening and discontinuity of the fibers at midsubstance. Empty intercondylar fossa is demonstrated; suggested complete ACL tear combined with interstitial tear at midsubstance.  
  Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Buckling PCL without definite abnormal SI  
  Anterior tibial translation is noted.  
  
 Medial compartment  
  Medial meniscus: Suspected meniscus tear at posterior horn as noted in sagittal PDFS images. Anterior and posterior meniscal root is still preserved. Articular cartilage is preserved.  
  Medial collateral ligament:  
  Superficial ligament: 0  
  Deep ligament: Grade 1 meniscofemoral ligament sprain. 
  Medial tibial plateau: Normal  
  Medial femoral condyle: Normal  
  
 Lateral compartment  
  Lateral meniscus: No discoid meniscus. No tear.  
  Iliotibial band: 0  
  Lateral collateral ligament (LCL): 0  
  Popliteus tendon: 0  
  Biceps femoris tendon: 0  
  Lateral tibial plateau: Normal  
  Lateral femoral condyle: Normal  
  Fibular head: Normal  
  
 Patellofemoral compartment  
  Quadriceps tendon: Normal  
  Patellar tendon: Normal  
  Medial patellar retinaculum: 0  
  Lateral patellar retinaculum: 0  
  
 Others  
  The surrounding musculature appears grossly unremarkable.  
  Neurovascular bundles are grossly intact  
  Some amount of effusion within patellofemoral joint to suprapatellar bursa is noted.  Complete ACL tear combined with interstitial tear at midsubstance.   
  Medial meniscus: Suspected medial meniscus tear at posterior horn. 
  Grade 1 meniscofemoral ligament sprain of deep ligament of medial collateral ligament.  
  Some amount of effusion within patellofemoral joint to suprapatellar bursa.

Medial compartment  
 - Medial meniscus:  
 -- High horizontal SI along anterior horn; suggested horizontal tear. 
 -- Vertical high SI at body of meniscus with deformed posterior horn and abnormal high SI at posterior root; suggested vertical tear at body of meniscus, with involvement of the posterior horn and suspected posterior root tear, with protrusion to anteromedial aspect. 
 - Medial collateral ligament: Fluid surrounding edematous MCL with high SI at proximal part of MCL; suggested sprain with inflammation. 
 - Medial gastrocnemius: Preserved.  
 - Semimembranosus tendon: Preserved.  
 - Semitendinosus tendon: Preserved.  
 - Pes anserine tendon: Preserved.  
 - Baker cyst: Present, measured about 3.4x1.7x4.2 cm, extending craniocaudally to the proximal leg. 
 - Synovial cysts at posteromedial aspect of the right knee joint with internal low SI on T1W; suggested calcified loose bodies. 
 - Grade-4 chondrosis at medial tibial plateau with adjacent mild subchondral bone edema, subchondral bone cysts (at femur aspect) is seen. Osteophyte is observed.  
  
 Lateral compartment  
 - Lateral meniscus: High vertical SI at anterior horn of lateral meniscus, extending to meniscal surface; suggested vertical tear. The body and posterior horn appears intact. 
 - Lateral collateral ligament: High SI along proximal part of LCL;  suggested ligament sprain. 
 - Popliteus tendon: High SI; suspected interstitial tear. Bursal cysts with fibrin and loose bodies along the popliteus muscle is seen; suggested bursitis. 
 - Poplitiofibular ligament: Preserved.  
 - Meniscofemoral ligament: Unidentifiable; suspected tear.  
 - Biceps femoris: Preserved.  
 - Iliotibial band: Intact.  
 - Lateral gastrocnemius: Intact.  
 - Grade-2 chondrosis of articular cartilage of weight baring area at lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau by evidence of focal defect. Osteophyte at lateral tibial plateau is shown. Focal bone marrow edema at superior tibiofibular joint is noted. 
  
 Patellofemoral joint  
 - The patellofemoral joint: Grade-3 chondrosis with focal defect at lateral aspect. Grade-3 chondrosis at femoral trochea. Osteophyte is also noted.  
 - Medial patellar retinaculum: Normal. 
 - Lateral patellar retinaculum: Normal.  
 - Quadriceps tendon, patella ligament are intact.  
  
 Central compartment  
 - ACL: Bright slit SI at mid part of ACL; suspected intrasubstance tear. 
 - PCL: Normal. 
  
 Others:  
 - Fluid within suprapatellar bursa, knee joint, infrapatellar bursa, and within the subcutaneous layer. Edematous fat pad surrounding right knee and prepatellar is noted.  
 - Neurovascular structure is unremarkable.   - Severe tri-compartmental osteoarthritis (OA) of right knee and PF joints.  
 - Severe chondrosis of the tibiofemoral and PF joints. 
 - Horizontal tear of anterior horn of medial meniscus. Vertical tear at body of meniscus, with involvement  of the posterior horn and suspected posterior root tear. 
 - Vertical tear at anterior horn of lateral meniscus. 
 - Suspected intrasubstance tear of ACL. 
 - Suspected interstitial tear of popliteus tendon and suspected tear of meniscofemoral ligament. 
 - Sprain of MCL, proximal part of LCL. 
 - Baker cyst and synovial cysts at posteromedial aspect of the right knee joint. 
 - Bursal cysts with fibrin and loose bodies along the popliteus muscle; suggested bursitis.

COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Ultrasound raise the possibility of meniscal tear.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The medial meniscus shows an inferiorly surfacing oblique tear at the junction of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with tiny adjacent meniscal cysts. There is slight peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The posterior root and anterior horn are intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

No patellofemoral subluxation. The patellar retinacula are intact. The TT-TG distance measures 11 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Scattered foci of mild chondrosis throughout the patellofemoral compartment. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis. There is mild to moderate medial femorotibial chondrosis with slight thinning of articular cartilage along the central weightbearing aspect of the condyle.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Inferiorly suspected complete tear of the junction of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with tiny adjacent parameniscal cyst and slight peripheral medial meniscal extrusion.
2. Subtle tricompartment chondrosis suggesting evolving mild osteoarthritis of the left knee.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Knee locking after trampoline injury. Associated swelling and buckling. Difficulty with knee flexion and extension. No prior surgery.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
The knee is imaged in borderline anterior drawer alignment. Osteochondral impaction injury at the posterolateral femoral condyle and severe osseous contusion at the sulcus terminalis at the lateral femoral condyle. Additional reciprocal focal severe osseous contusions at the anterior medial tibial plateau, medial femoral condyle, and posterior medial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is otherwise normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Trace joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Small vertical tear at the peripheral aspect of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, compatible with a meniscal ramp lesion.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Small complex tear at the posterior horn extending into the root. No extrusion. 
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness chondrosis at the medial patellar facet. Chondral heterogeneity at the lateral patellar facet.The trochlear cartilage is preserved.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Near complete-complete tear of the more distal fibers.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Grade 1 sprain.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: Mild proximal patellar tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Mild edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. Patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 9 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Soft tissue edema at the posterior aspect of the knee.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Findings of a recent pivot shift mechanism injury, including: 
*	Near complete to complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) at its more distal fibers.
*	Small complex tear at the posterior root of the lateral meniscus.
*	Small vertical tear at the peripheral aspect of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, compatible with a meniscal ramp lesion.
*	Grade 1 sprain of the medial collateral ligament (MCL).
*	Osteochondral impaction injury at the posterolateral femoral condyle, severe osseous contusion at the sulcus terminalis of the lateral femoral condyle, and additional reciprocal severe contusions at the anterior medial tibial plateau, medial femoral condyle, and posterior medial tibial plateau.

2.	Patellofemoral chondrosis with findings suggestive of active lateral patellofemoral maltracking.
3.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis.
